hey can u help me understand this part of an nda i just got? it says: "The Receiving Party shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Disclosing Party from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of or resulting from any breach of this Agreement or any unauthorized use of the Confidential Information by the Receiving Party or its Representatives." basically what does this mean for me if i mess up?

This clause is essentially a **financial and legal safety net** for the other side. If you (the Receiving Party) or anyone acting on your behalf (your Representatives—employees, contractors, etc.) breach the NDA or misuse the confidential info, you’re on the hook for *everything* that flows from that mistake. That includes direct losses, legal fees, court costs, and even indirect damages—basically, you’d be paying to make them whole, plus their lawyers’ bills.

It’s a heavy burden, but it’s also standard in NDAs. The key is to avoid the trigger: don’t share the info, don’t use it beyond the stated purpose, and make sure your team knows the rules. If you do slip up, this clause means you’re not just apologizing—you’re writing a check.

**Your practical takeaway:** Before signing, check if the clause is mutual (both sides indemnify each other) or one-sided. If it’s one-sided, try to narrow it to “gross negligence or willful misconduct” rather than any breach. And keep a tight internal process for handling the info—compliance is your shield.

Yes, you’re essentially the one holding the bag—the clause makes you responsible for your Representatives’ actions as if they were your own. If a sub-contractor you bring in leaks the confidential info, you’re the one who has to indemnify the Disclosing Party for the resulting losses, legal fees, and any other costs. It doesn’t matter if the leak was accidental or if the sub-contractor acted against your instructions; the contract looks to you as the party who brought them into the fold.

That said, you’re not *totally* without recourse in the real world—you could sue the sub-contractor yourself for breach of contract or negligence, but that’s a separate fight. The NDA’s indemnity clause means you pay first, then chase them later. So, practically, you’d want to:  
- Have your own sub-contractor agreements with similar indemnity and confidentiality terms.  
- Vet them carefully, maybe even require them to sign a direct NDA with the Disclosing Party.  
- Limit their access to only what’s strictly necessary—minimize the chance of a leak.

**1. Look for the “catch-all” words.** Words like “any and all,” “arising out of or resulting from,” and “including but not limited to” are red flags.
